ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.DICT.mastery: Puts words in alphabetical order (using the second and third letters when the first match), uses guide words to find the page, and picks the right meaning of a word from its entry, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.mastery: Chooses the dictionary, junior encyclopaedia, atlas, newspaper or timetable for what the child needs to find out, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.mastery: Chooses or writes a, an or the (a before a consonant sound, an before a vowel sound, the for a known or named thing, no article for things in general) and finds the one wrong article in a short note, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.mastery: Says which piece of information belongs in a box of a school, clinic or library form (name, date of birth, class, address, parent contact), in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.mastery: Finds an answer that is written in the text (who, what, where, when) and says whether a statement is true, false or not stated, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: choose what can be worked out
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.INFE.mastery: Works out what is not written but is shown by clues (why a person felt or did something) and does not copy a sentence, go against the text or go too far, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.mastery: Picks the meaning of a new word from the sentences around it, and the words that give the clue, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.mastery: Forms the plural of regular nouns (-s, -es after s, x, ch, sh, -ies after a consonant and y, -ves for knife and leaf) and does not add -s to a number-plus-noun that is already plural, in 8 of 10 new items.
Writes the plural of man, woman, child, foot, tooth, mouse, person, sheep and fish and does not add -s or a second plural ending, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.mastery: Picks the polite word or phrase for a situation (asking, thanking, apologising, refusing) and does not choose a command or a rude answer, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.mastery: Builds and recognises polite requests and offers (May I go out, please? Could you help me? Would you like some tea?) with the plain verb after May I and Could you, in whole sentences, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T4_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.mastery: Uses the words of first aid (bandage, wound, bruise, sprain, ambulance, first aid kit) in the right sentence, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G4.READIN.T4_INTENSIVE_READING_VI.V.mastery: Finds a detail in a notice, table or timetable written in words and numbers, and says what the visual is for, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.mastery: Chooses the subject form before the verb and the object form after the verb or a small word, and does not repeat a noun with a pronoun (Wanjiru she is tall), in 8 of 10 new items.
Writes mine, yours, his, hers, ours or theirs when no noun follows, my, your, her, our or their before a noun, and never writes your's, her's or our's, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.mastery: Names and orders the parts of a friendly letter (address, date, greeting, body, closing, name) and the punctuation of the greeting and closing, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T5_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.N.mastery: Uses the words of nutrition (protein, vitamins, carbohydrates, balanced diet, fibre, nutrients) in the right sentence, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G4.READIN.T5_EXTENSIVE_READING.SCAN.mastery: Finds a number, time, price or name by looking for the key word in the question, not by reading every word, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.mastery: Names the describing word that tells more about a noun (tall girl, red bus) and does not pick the noun, the verb or an adverb, in 8 of 10 new items.
Puts size before shape before the noun (a big round ball) and never puts the adjective after the noun as in Kiswahili, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.mastery: Says what the title, beginning, middle and end of a narrative tell (characters and setting, the problem, what happens, how it ends), in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.PARAG.mastery: Finds the topic sentence and puts four jumbled sentences in the order that makes a clear paragraph, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T6_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.I.mastery: Uses email, inbox, attachment, subject, password, website, search and download in the right sentence, and tells safe online habits from unsafe ones, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.mastery: Uses many and few with things you can count and much and little with things you cannot count, in statements and questions, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.S.mastery: Uses some in positive sentences, any in questions and negatives, a lot of and enough before the noun, and does not put enough after the noun, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T6_CREATIVE_WRITING.PICTU.mastery: Orders four pictures, given in words, so that the story makes sense, and picks the sentence that tells one picture in the past tense, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.mastery: Uses the regular (-ed) and irregular (went, ate, saw) past forms when the time is past, and uses the present forms for habits and facts, in short dialogues, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.mastery: Writes am, is or are plus the -ing verb for an action happening now, with the right form of be and the right spelling of -ing, in 8 of 10 new items.
